Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life

heaven noun

the dwelling of God

also the kingdom of heaven, paradise, go to heaven, in heaven, for heaven’s sake

classical

Vulg. Mt. 6.9
M-O s.v. heaven

caelum, caelī n.

noun, second declension

The sky, and the dwelling of the gods and of God. The Church often uses the plural, caelī, after the Hebrew (quī es in caelīs; Lewis & Short); the kingdom of heaven is rēgnum caelōrum. For heaven’s sake! is obsecrō (Traupman 327).

Examples

  • Pater noster, quī es in caelīs, sānctificētur nōmen tuum.

    Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.Vulg. Mt. 6.9

  • tālium est rēgnum caelōrum

    of such is the kingdom of heaven (said over a sleeping child)Aug. Conf. 1.19.30

  • hodiē mēcum eris in paradīsō

    today you will be with me in paradiseVulg. Lc. 23.43

Other words

  • paradīsus, paradīsī m. — paradise

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Lc. 23.43; Tert. Apol. 47 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. heaven

    Greek παράδεισος, a park (Gell.); the garden of Eden (paradīsus voluptātis, Gen. 2.15), and the dwelling of the blessed (Lewis & Short).

See also sky, God, soul, the Ascension.

SourcesLewis & Short: caelum · Lewis & Short: paradisus
